title: Learning Multi-Agent Orchestration:Higher-Order Interactions in Policy Improvement
abstract: arXiv:2611.07495v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Learned orchestration has emerged as a promising paradigm for large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems, in which a central orchestrator selects agents and controls the information they receive throughout a task. Despite rapid empirical progress, existing methods train the orchestrator by crediting each decision with its own advantage, implicitly assuming that the other decisions in the episode stay fixed. This assumption fails in orchestration, where the contribution of each decision to the final outcome depends on the decisions preceding it, so the gain of a joint update is not the sum of its per-decision effects. To address this challenge, we introduce \textbf{IAPO}, an interaction-aware policy optimization framework that explicitly accounts for interactions among decisions. Specifically, IAPO exactly decomposes the performance difference between two policies into the effects of individual decisions and their interactions,

translated_title: 学习多智能体编排：策略提升中的高阶交互
translated_abstract: 学习型编排已成为基于大语言模型（LLM）的多智能体系统中一种颇具前景的范式，其中一个中央编排器在任务执行过程中选择智能体并控制它们所接收的信息。尽管实证进展迅速，现有方法在训练编排器时，是将每个决策单独归因于其自身的优势，隐含地假设回合中的其他决策保持不变。这一假设在编排任务中并不成立，因为每个决策对最终结果的贡献取决于其之前的决策，因此联合更新的收益并不等于各决策单独效果之和。为应对这一挑战，我们提出了IAPO，一种能够显式考虑决策之间交互的交互感知策略优化框架。具体而言，IAPO将两个策略之间的性能差异精确分解为个体决策的效果及其交互效果。
tldr: 提出交互感知策略优化框架IAPO，通过将两个策略间的性能差异精确分解为个体决策效果及其交互效果，显式建模LLM多智能体编排中决策之间的高阶依赖关系，从而改进编排器的训练。
en_tdlr: IAPO is an interaction-aware policy optimization framework that exactly decomposes the performance difference between two policies into individual decision effects and their interactions, explicitly modeling higher-order dependencies among decisions to improve orchestrator training in LLM-based multi-agent orchestration.
